q: In a standard 1v4 Trial, how many Generators spawn on the map?
x: There are more possible spawn spots than Generators, so where they appear changes from Trial to Trial.
evidence: A regular ranked Trial spawns a total of 7 Generators in predetermined locations throughout the environment.

q: How many Generators must Survivors repair to power the Exit Gates in a standard Trial?
x: In Custom Games with fewer Survivors, the target drops by one per missing Survivor, down to just 2 for a solo Survivor.
evidence: Survivors must repair a total of 5 Generators in order to power the Exit Gates .

q: How long does one Survivor take to repair a Generator with no perks or items?
x: Teaming up helps, but each extra Survivor adds a 15% efficiency penalty, so even four players still need about 41 seconds.
evidence: 1 Survivor 0 % 100 % = 1 c/s 1 c/s (1 x 1 c/s) 90 seconds

q: What does a Great Skill Check give you while repairing a Generator?
x: A Good Skill Check, in the see-through part of the zone, gives only 50 Bloodpoints and no bonus progress.
evidence: Grants 300 Bloodpoints and a +1 % Progression bonus for Repair actions.

q: What happens when you fail a Skill Check while repairing a Generator?
o: It loses all of its progress
x: The bang alerts the Killer with a Loud Noise Notification, and the Generator can't gain progress for 3 seconds.
evidence: If they fail at a Skill Check , the Repair progress instead receives a Progression penalty of -10 % and the Generator explodes, triggering a Loud Noise Notification for the Killer.

q: By default, how much progress does a Generator instantly lose when the Killer kicks it?
x: The kick takes 1.8 seconds, and the Generator then keeps slowly regressing until a Survivor works on it again.
evidence: By default, kicking a Generator takes 1.8 seconds and causes it to lose an immediate -5 % of its total Progression.

q: How many Regression Events can one Generator suffer before the Entity stops the Killer damaging it?
x: From the fourth Regression Event onwards, growing spikes appear around the Generator to warn the Killer the limit is near.
evidence: Each Generator has a limit of 8 times that it can experience a Regression Event.

q: How long does each of the first two Hook Stages last by default?
x: Stage one is the Summoning Phase and stage two is the Struggle Phase. Reaching the third stage means instant sacrifice.
evidence: Summoning Phase 70 seconds ; 100 to 51 %

q: What is the default chance of a self-unhook attempt succeeding on the first Hook Stage?
x: Each failed try costs 20 seconds. Since Patch 9.0.0, tries only work in special cases, such as when just 2 Survivors remain.
evidence: If available, attempt a Self-Unhook , which has a default Success Chance of 4 % per attempt.

q: How long must a carried Survivor wiggle in total to break free from the Killer?
x: Wiggle time adds up over the carry. It exists so Killers can't haul a Survivor to the Basement from anywhere on the map.
evidence: If the carried Survivors manages to wiggle for a total of 16 seconds (accumulative) before the Killer can reach a Hook , the latter will lose their grip on the Survivor, setting them free.

q: Which protections does a Survivor get for 10 seconds after being unhooked?
x: These Unhook Protections end early if the Survivor performs a Conspicuous Action, like repairing under the Killer's nose.
evidence: The Unhook Protections encompass the following effects for 10 seconds : 10 % Haste Status Effect Endurance Status Effect Elusive Status Effect

q: What does a hooked Survivor get once the anti-camp Resolve Bar is full?
o: An extra minute on the Hook
x: The bar fills while the Killer lingers within 16 metres of the Hook. The whole system switches off once the Exit Gates are powered.
evidence: Once the Resolve Bar is filled, the Hooked Survivor is granted a guaranteed Self-Unhook attempt.

q: How long does it take a Survivor to open an Exit Gate?
x: Three red lights on the switch light up at 25, 50 and 75%, so everyone can tell how close the Gate is to opening.
evidence: It takes Survivors 20 seconds to open an Exit Gate .

q: How long is the Endgame Collapse timer when it starts?
x: It ticks at half speed while Survivors are downed or hooked, so the Collapse can last up to 4 minutes.
evidence: A timer of 2 minutes will appear at the top of the screen, slowly ticking down.

q: Besides an Exit Gate being opened, what starts the Endgame Collapse?
x: The Endgame Collapse and the Killer's ability to close the Hatch both arrived in Patch 2.7.0.
evidence: The Hatch was closed by the Killer.

q: When does the Hatch open by itself?
a: When only one Survivor is left
o: When the Exit Gates are powered
x: It was originally known as the 'Black Lock'. If the Killer closes it, a Key can open it again.
evidence: The Hatch only becomes visible, and automatically opens, when there is only a single Survivor left alive in the Trial.

q: How many Totems spawn in every Trial?
x: They all start as Dull Totems unless the Killer brings Hex Perks, which turn some of them into Hex Totems.
evidence: All Trials spawn with 5 Totems in random locations, usually hidden against environmental objects and in nooks and crannies.

q: How long does cleansing a Totem take by default?
x: Unlike a Generator, a Totem keeps no partial progress: get interrupted and you start over.
evidence: Survivors can walk up to either type of Totem and perform the Cleansing interaction, which by default takes 14 seconds to complete.

q: How can you tell a Hex Totem apart from a Dull Totem?
o: It glows with a blue shimmer
x: A blue shimmer means a Boon Totem instead. Destroying a Hex Totem sets off a thunderclap the whole map can hear.
evidence: Hex Totems are a special kind of Totem, identifiable by the lit candles underneath them.

q: What is the Killer's interaction with a Boon Totem called?
x: It takes just 1 second and turns the Boon back into a Dull Totem. Survivors can't cleanse a Boon Totem at all.
evidence: A Killer can walk up to any Boon Totem and snuff it out, which takes 1 second to complete.

q: How many Chests spawn in a Trial by default?
x: One of them always spawns down in the Basement. Offerings and Perks can push the count anywhere from 1 to 13.
evidence: By default, 3 Chests will spawn each Trial.

q: Which two Item types are the most common finds in Chests?
x: Each turns up about 37% of the time, while Maps are the rarest find at around 2%.
evidence: Med-Kits 37 % 23 % Toolboxes 37 % 37 %

q: How long is the Killer stunned when a Survivor drops a Pallet on them?
x: A Pallet stun also earns the Survivor a hefty amount of Bloodpoints in the Boldness category.
evidence: If a Killer is inside the area of a Pallet and a Survivor pulls it down, they will be pushed back and get stunned for 2 seconds , obstructing their vision as their camera tilts.

q: After how many vaults in one chase does the Entity block a Window for that Survivor?
x: The block lasts 30 seconds and only affects that Survivor. It was added to stop endless 'infinite' loops.
evidence: If a Survivor vaults the same Window multiple times in the same Chase sequence, The Entity will block it after the third vault and leave it blocked to that particular Survivor for the next 30 seconds .

q: Which Status Effect does a Locker give a hiding Survivor, stopping them from reading Auras?
x: The upside: a Locker also hides the Survivor's own Aura from the Killer and from other Survivors.
evidence: since the Locker afflicts them with the Blindness Status Effect when inside.

q: Which special Health State sits between Injured and Dying?
x: A Deep Wounded Survivor must Mend before a bleed-out timer runs out, or they fall into the Dying State.
evidence: There is also a special fourth state situated in-between the Injured State and the Dying State : Deep Wound

q: What is the longest a Survivor can stay in the Dying State before bleeding out?
x: Since Patch 9.2.0, downed Survivors recover on their own while staying still, up to 95%.
evidence: limiting the amount of time they can remain in the Dying State before death to a cumulative maximum duration of 240 seconds .

q: How many Charges does it take to heal a Survivor by one Health State?
x: It was 12 Charges until Patch 2.3.0. Two Survivors healing a third together double the healing speed.
evidence: It takes 16 Charges to heal a Survivors for the equivalent of 1 Health State .

q: What does the Exposed Status Effect do to a Survivor?
x: Despite the name, Exposed has never revealed a Survivor's Aura. That is a common myth among new players.
evidence: Survivors suffering from Exposed will suffer double-damage when hit by a Basic Attack , which immediately puts them into the Dying State .

q: What can a Survivor with the Broken Status Effect not do?
x: Broken is a Survivor-only debuff. You can still be picked up from the Dying State, just not healed back to Healthy.
evidence: Survivors suffering from Broken are unable to be healed or heal themselves past the Injured State .

q: Which Status Effect stops a Survivor from hearing the Killer's Terror Radius?
x: Oblivious Survivors also miss the Heartbeat warning, though they can still hear the Chase Music once a chase starts.
evidence: Survivors suffering from Oblivious are unable to perceive the Killer's Terror Radius and also do not hear the Heartbeat warning of the Killer's proximity.

q: Besides the Terror Radius, what does the Undetectable Status Effect hide?
x: It also blocks the Killer's own Aura from being revealed to Survivors.
evidence: Killers benefitting from Undetectable are granted several Stealth mechanics: Suppresses the Terror Radius Suppresses the Red Stain

q: How long must a chase last before the Killer gains Bloodlust Tier I?
x: Each tier adds 0.2 m/s, up to Tier III at 35 seconds. Hitting a Survivor or breaking a Pallet wipes it out.
evidence: I 15 seconds +0.2 m/s 4.6 m/s or 115 %

q: What was the classic Terror Radius size for Killers who walk at 4.6 m/s?
x: Slower 4.4 m/s Killers got 24 metres. Nowadays stealth, mobility and ranged attacks also shape a Killer's Terror Radius.
evidence: 32 metres for 115-Killers (Walking speed of 4.6 m/s )

q: Who can see the Red Stain that glows in front of a Killer?
x: The Killer can't see their own Stain, so crafty Killers walk backwards or sideways around corners to hide where they face.
evidence: Survivors are constantly able to see The Red Stain on the floor in front of the Killer, unless it is hidden by the use of cloaking-Perks or Powers.

q: In a normal 4-Survivor Trial, what is each Survivor's default chance of becoming the Obsession?
x: The Obsession mechanic arrived with the Halloween Chapter, echoing how Michael Myers is obsessed with Laurie.
evidence: In regular ranked Trials with 4 Survivors, this creates a default chance of 25 % (1 in 4)

q: Since Patch 8.3.0, which Survivor can every Killer Mori without an Offering?
x: This base-kit Finisher Mori took over the job of the Cypress Memento Mori Offering, which was then retired.
evidence: With the implementation of the Finisher Mori in Patch 8.3.0 , the ability to kill the Last Survivor Standing has become base-kit for all Killers.

q: What does the Latin phrase 'Memento Mori' mean?
x: Killing a Survivor by hand is called a Mori, after the Memento Mori Offerings that first allowed it.
evidence: "Memento Mori" is a Latin idiom, which translates to "Remember Death/Remember Mortality" .

q: What is the highest Level a character can reach in the Bloodweb before prestiging?
x: Each finished Bloodweb adds one Level. After you clear the Level 50 web, a single Prestige node appears.
evidence: Levels are represented with a number ranging from 1 to 50 .

q: What is the highest Prestige level a character can reach?
x: Before the Patch 6.1.0 rework, you could only prestige a character 3 times.
evidence: Prestige is represented with various crests and ranges from 0 to 100 .

q: What does reaching Prestige 1 on a character unlock?
x: Prestige 2 and 3 upgrade those Perks to Tiers II and III, and blood-stained cosmetics start at Prestige 4.
evidence: Unlocks that Character's Unique Perks at Tier I for immediate use on all Characters, automatically adding them to their inventories.

q: At which Levels does a new character unlock Perk Slots 2, 3 and 4?
x: Every character starts with just 1 Perk Slot and can equip up to 4 Perks once all slots are open.
evidence: Additional Perk Slots are successively unlocked at Levels 5, 10, and 15 of the Bloodweb .

q: At which Bloodweb Level does the Entity wake up and start eating nodes?
x: It likes to grab the rarest nodes first, so buy the things you really want early.
evidence: Players can purchase Nodes undisturbed until they progress a Character's Bloodweb to Level 10 , at which point The Entity awakens and starts to interfere.

q: What is the most Bloodpoints you can earn in one scoring category in a single Trial?
x: With four categories that makes 40,000 per Trial before Offerings. The category cap was 8,000 until Patch 6.1.0.
evidence: During the Trial, Players may only accumulate a maximum of 10,000 Bloodpoints in each of the four Scoring Categories, for a maximum of 40,000 Bloodpoints .

q: What is the current cap on Bloodpoints you can hold from Trials?
x: Patch 8.6.0 raised it from 2 million, after the higher cap was tested during the Blood Moon 2025 event.
evidence: Bloodpoints are capped at 5,000,000 Bloodpoints for all Bloodpoints gained from Trials and those awarded from collecting completed Tome Challenges.

q: Survivor Bloodpoint Offerings are named after flowers. What are the Killer ones named after?
x: Each name fits its category: the Shrike, a bird that impales its prey, stands for the Sacrifice category.
evidence: The original Offerings for Bonus Bloodpoints in a specific Category are all named after flowering plants (Survivor Offerings) and birds (Killer Offerings)

q: When does the Shrine of Secrets refresh each week?

evidence: The Shrine of Secrets resets every Tuesday at 15:00 UTC (GMT+0) .

q: How many Perks does the Shrine of Secrets offer at a time?
x: It is always 2 Survivor and 2 Killer Perks, and a Perk can't come back for at least the next 3 Shrines.
evidence: The Shrine features a selection of 4 Unique Perks (always 2 for Survivors and 2 for Killers).

q: What do you get for buying a Shrine Perk you already own at Tier III?

evidence: It should be noted that purchasing a Perk that is already unlocked at Tier III grants 100,000 Bloodpoints instead.

evidence: Iridescent Shards were the first new currency added to the Game.

q: How many Iridescent Shards does a newer original (non-licensed) character cost?

evidence: Original Characters (meaning 'non-licensed') can be bought for 9,000 Iridescent Shards .

q: How many Auric Cells does the Rift Pass premium track cost?
x: Finishing the pass pays all 1,000 back, thanks to 25 to 50 Auric Cell rewards spread along the track.
evidence: its Rewards will not be granted unless Players have purchased the Battle-Pass, which costs 1,000 Auric Cells .

q: Since Patch 8.7.0, how many Rift Fragments does each Rift Pass tier need?

evidence: Each Rift Pass Tier requires 100 Rift Fragments

evidence: Any left-over Trinkets not spent on Cosmetics are automatically converted into Bloodpoints .

q: Since September 2021, what does DBD use to decide who you are matched with?
x: Grades no longer affect matchmaking at all. They just track your monthly season and pay out Bloodpoints.
evidence: Since 8 September 2021, Dead by Daylight uses a hidden scoring system for its matchmaking, known as the Skill-Based Matchmaking Rating (SBMM) or more commonly as just Matchmaking Rating (MMR).

q: Which Survivor Emblem grades how much you pushed the main objective?

evidence: The Lightbringer Emblem grades how much the Player participated in progressing the main objective as a Survivor.

q: In the 2v8 mode, how many Generators spawn on the map?
x: Survivors must repair 8 of them, but each one needs only 70 Charges instead of the usual 90.

q: When did the 2v8 mode first become playable?
x: The first run lasted from 25 July to 15 August 2024, and the mode has come back every few months since.
evidence: The first iteration of this Game Mode was available between 25 July and 15 August 2024.

q: In 2v8, what do players pick instead of regular Perks, Items and Add-ons?

q: What could Killer players do for the first time thanks to 2v8?
a: Queue up with a Killer friend
o: Talk to Survivors in voice chat
x: The queue can't be mixed, so friends must play on the same side in a 2v8 Trial.
evidence: 2v8 premiered the ability for a Killer Player to queue up with a friend to play a Trial together, taking on the role of the second Killer for the Trial.

q: Which Status Effect exists only in the 2v8 mode?

evidence: Survivors suffering from Revealed have their Aura revealed to both Killers in the 2v8 Game Mode, to which this Status Effect is exclusive.

q: What does the Lights Out Modifier do to Trials?

evidence: Lights Out modifies the Gameplay Loop by drastically reducing the visibility and brightness on its selected Maps and focusing on stealth- and horror-elements.

q: What is special about your Perks in the Chaos Shuffle Modifier?
o: They are swapped with the Killer's
They are locked at Tier I
x: All four Perk Slots are open and every Perk is Tier III, even ones you have not unlocked yet.
evidence: causing all five Players to enter the Trial with a fully randomised set of Perks .

q: What was the Custom Game mode originally called?

evidence: Custom Game , originally known as Kill Your Friends and abbreviated as "KYF" , is one of 3 permanently available Game Modes featured in Dead by Daylight .

evidence: This iteration of Haunted by Daylight sees the removal of The Void mechanic that has been present since Haunted by Daylight 2023 .

q: What has DBD's winter event been called since 2021?

q: What does a Blood Hunt event do?
x: Blood Hunts are usually weekend events lasting about four days, starting at 15:00 UTC.

q: Which Survivor do you control in the Survivor tutorial?
